nodes.label: Resource Planning in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Three stages: identification and inventory of resources, evolving planning structure with technology and skills, matching resource development with national development plans. Resource-rich states not necessarily developed.

nodes.label: India's Land Resources
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Total area 3.28 million sq km. 43% plain, 30% mountains, 27% plateaus. Net sown area 46.24%. Forest 22.57%. Land under non-agricultural use 5.57%. Fallow 7.91%. Culturable waste 4.42%.

nodes.label: Indian Soil Types
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Six major types: Alluvial (most widespread, entire northern plains), Black/Regur (Deccan trap, ideal for cotton), Red and Yellow (crystalline rocks), Laterite (heavy rainfall areas, leached), Arid (sandy, high salt), Forest/Mountain.

nodes.label: Alluvial Soil
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Most widespread and important. Deposited by rivers. Two types: old alluvium Bangar (higher up, less fertile, has kankar) and new alluvium Khadar (lower, more fertile, renewed by floods). Rich in potash, poor in phosphorus.

nodes.label: Black Soil (Regur)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Also called Regur. Made up of lava flows of Deccan trap. Covers NW Deccan Plateau, Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh. Rich in calcium, magnesium, potash, lime. Ideal for cotton. Self-ploughing: develops cracks when dry.

nodes.label: Red and Yellow Soil
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Develop on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall. Red colour from iron diffusion in crystalline/metamorphic rocks. Found in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, southern Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, NE hills.

nodes.label: Laterite Soil
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Develops in high temperature and heavy rainfall areas by leaching. Humus content low as high temperature decomposition is fast. Found in Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, MP hills. Good for tea, coffee, cashew after manuring.

nodes.label: Arid/Desert Soil
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Sandy and saline. High salt content due to high evaporation. Lacks humus and moisture. Kankar (calcium) layer restricts water infiltration. Found in western Rajasthan. Becomes fertile with proper irrigation.

nodes.label: Soil Erosion
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Gully erosion makes land unfit (bad land/ravines in Chambal). Sheet erosion removes top soil. Wind erosion in arid areas. Running water main agent. Deforestation, overgrazing, mining, construction accelerate it.

nodes.label: Forest and Mountain Soil
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Found in hilly and mountainous areas where sufficient rain. Heterogeneous, changes with altitude. Loamy and silty in valley sides. In upper slopes, humus content high, acidic. Low in snowbound areas.

nodes.label: Land Degradation in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: 130 million hectares degraded. Mining in Jharkhand-Odisha-MP. Over-irrigation in Punjab-Haryana causing waterlogging and salinity. Overgrazing in Gujarat-Rajasthan-MP. Deforestation reduces protective cover.

nodes.label: Joint Forest Management
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Government and local communities jointly manage forests. Odisha pioneered in 1988 with local communities protecting degraded sal forests. Communities get non-timber products and share timber revenue.

nodes.label: Chipko and Appiko Movements
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Chipko (1974, Uttarakhand, led by Sunderlal Bahuguna): people hugged trees against contractors. Appiko (1983, Karnataka): similar southern movement. Both grassroots environmental conservation movements.

nodes.label: Community Participation in Conservation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Beyond government programs, communities manage forests (Van Panchayats in Uttarakhand). Beej Bachao Andolan in Tehri for seed conservation. Nature clubs and eco-development committees in many states.

nodes.label: Dam Controversies
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Opposition due to: displacement of tribals, environmental destruction, sedimentation, fragmentation of rivers, affects aquatic life, waterlogging and salinity. Narmada Bachao Andolan against Sardar Sarovar Dam.

nodes.label: Hirakud Dam
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: On Mahanadi river in Odisha. One of longest dams in the world (4.8 km). Built in 1957. Controls floods, provides irrigation and power to Odisha.

nodes.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Movement against Sardar Sarovar Dam on Narmada river, led by Medha Patkar. Issues: displacement of tribals, environmental concerns, inadequate rehabilitation. Highlighted social justice in development.

nodes.label: Inter-State Water Disputes
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Major disputes over sharing of river waters between states. Krishna-Godavari between Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP. Kaveri between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Tribunals set up for resolution.

nodes.label: Indian Agriculture
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Primary activity, two-thirds of population dependent. Three cropping seasons: Kharif (June-Sep: rice, jowar, bajra, cotton, jute, sugarcane), Rabi (Oct-March: wheat, barley, peas, gram, mustard), Zaid (summer: watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber).

nodes.label: Green Revolution
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Introduced in 1960s, focused on HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, irrigation. Primarily in wheat and rice. Made India self-sufficient in foodgrains. Concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, western UP. Led to regional disparities.

nodes.label: Rice in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Kharif crop. Needs high temperature (above 25C), high humidity, 100cm+ rainfall. Grown in alluvial and clayey soil. Major areas: WB, UP, Andhra, Punjab, TN. India second largest producer after China.

nodes.label: Wheat in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Rabi crop. Needs cool growing season (10-15C), bright sunshine at ripening. 50-75cm rainfall. Loamy soil. Main areas: Punjab, Haryana, UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan. Second most important cereal after rice.

nodes.label: Cotton in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Kharif crop. Needs high temperature, light rainfall, 210 frost-free days. Black soil ideal. Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, Karnataka, AP, TN, Punjab, Haryana. India third largest producer. Supports textile industry.

nodes.label: Sugarcane in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Tropical and subtropical crop. Needs hot humid climate with 75-100cm rainfall. Rich loamy soil. Major: UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka, TN, AP, Gujarat. India second largest producer after Brazil. Used for sugar, gur, alcohol.

nodes.label: Tea in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Plantation crop. Needs warm moist frost-free climate year-round, frequent showers, well-drained loamy soil, gentle slopes. Labour intensive. Major: Assam, Darjeeling (WB), Nilgiris, Kerala. India largest producer and exporter.

nodes.label: Coffee in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Grown on hill slopes in shade. Needs warm moist climate with temperature 15-28C. Well-drained loamy soil. Mostly Arabica variety. Major: Karnataka (Coorg), Kerala, TN. Initial cultivation introduced by Arabs in Baba Budan Hills.

nodes.label: Pulses in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Major source of protein. India largest producer and consumer. Crops: tur/arhar, urad, moong, masoor, peas, gram. Grown as rotation crops to fix nitrogen and restore soil fertility. MP, UP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Karnataka.

nodes.label: Oilseeds in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Groundnut (most important, accounts for half of total), rapeseed-mustard, sesame, soyabean, sunflower, linseed, castor. India largest producer of oilseeds. Used for cooking, medicine, industry.

nodes.label: Rubber in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Equatorial crop grown in tropical and sub-tropical areas. Needs moist warm climate with above 200cm rainfall. Kerala leading producer (90% of India's rubber), followed by TN, Karnataka, Andaman-Nicobar.

nodes.label: Kharif and Rabi Seasons
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Kharif: sown at beginning of SW monsoon (June), harvested September-October. Rabi: sown beginning of winter (October), harvested March-April. Zaid: short summer season between rabi and kharif.

nodes.label: Food Security and MSP
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Government announces Minimum Support Price for crops. National Food Security Mission for rice, wheat, pulses. Public Distribution System ensures food reaches poor. Buffer stock maintained by FCI.

nodes.label: Institutional Reforms in Agriculture
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Abolition of zamindari, consolidation of holdings, cooperation, Bhoodan-Gramdan movement by Vinoba Bhave. Green Revolution, White Revolution (Operation Flood). Kisan Credit Cards, crop insurance, MSP.

nodes.label: Mineral Conservation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Minerals are non-renewable, finite resources. Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act 1957. Need to use improved technology, reduce wastage, recycle metals. Find substitutes for scarce minerals.

nodes.label: Cement Industry
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Essential for construction. India second largest producer. Raw materials: limestone, silica, alumina, gypsum. Deregulated in 1989 leading to expansion. Major: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, MP, AP, Chhattisgarh.

nodes.label: Indian Railways
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Asia's largest and world's 4th largest network. 68000+ km of routes. 16 zones. Lifeline of nation carrying 8 billion+ passengers yearly. Konkan Railway: engineering marvel (Ratnagiri to Mangalore). Broad, metre, narrow gauges being unified.

nodes.label: India's International Trade
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Exports: gems, jewellery, petroleum products, IT services, textiles, chemicals, leather, agricultural products. Imports: petroleum, gold, electronics, machinery, fertilisers. Unfavourable balance of trade. WTO membership.

nodes.label: Big Bang Theory
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Theory explaining the origin of the universe. Suggests the universe expanded from a singularity about 13.7 billion years ago. Initially all matter was concentrated; expansion continues today. Supported by cosmic microwave background radiation and redshift observations.

nodes.label: Geological Time Scale
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Chronological framework dividing Earth's 4.6 billion year history into eons, eras, periods, and epochs. Major eons: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (Precambrian), and Phanerozoic. Phanerozoic divided into Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic eras based on fossil records.
nodes.chapter_title: Origin and Evolution of the Earth

nodes.label: Precambrian
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Longest span of geological time covering from Earth's formation (4.6 bya) to 541 mya. Encompasses Hadean, Archean, and Proterozoic eons. Saw formation of continental crust, origin of life, and first multicellular organisms. Rocks of this age form shield areas and cratons.
nodes.chapter_title: Origin and Evolution of the Earth

nodes.label: Paleozoic Era
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Era from 541-252 mya meaning 'ancient life'. Periods include Cambrian, Ordovician, Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous, and Permian. Saw Cambrian explosion of marine life, first land plants, insects, amphibians, and reptiles. Ended with the largest mass extinction (Permian-Triassic).
nodes.chapter_title: Origin and Evolution of the Earth

nodes.label: Mesozoic Era
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Era from 252-66 mya meaning 'middle life'. Known as the Age of Reptiles/Dinosaurs. Periods: Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous. Pangaea broke apart during this era. Ended with the K-Pg extinction event (asteroid impact) that wiped out non-avian dinosaurs.
nodes.chapter_title: Origin and Evolution of the Earth

nodes.label: Cenozoic Era
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Current era from 66 mya to present meaning 'recent life'. Known as the Age of Mammals. Himalayas and Alps formed during this era. Periods: Paleogene, Neogene, Quaternary. Quaternary includes Pleistocene (ice ages) and Holocene (current epoch). Humans evolved in this era.
nodes.chapter_title: Origin and Evolution of the Earth

nodes.label: Star Formation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Stars form from condensation of gases (mainly hydrogen) in nebulae. Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium begins when core temperature rises sufficiently. Massive stars end as supernovae, creating heavier elements. The sun is a medium-sized star about 4.6 billion years old.
